title: Cold-sequence hypotheses — Atelier
content:
Note to self: use 'atelier' frame — craft the sequence like a short studio where we iterate quickly. This is rough: hypotheses, subject lines, 6-touch cadence, call script kernels, and a lightweight pilot offer for Hearthline Commerce (target vertical: mid-market commerce platform, strong retail integrations).

Account snapshot (quick brain-dump):
- Company: Hearthline Commerce (not in CRM yet; flagged from webinar attendee list).
- Size: ~200 employees, Series B, HQ SF.
- Tech signals: runs microservices on k8s, uses Redis, Postgres; indicated interest in LLM features for chat + search on ecommerce catalog.
- Decision makers: Dir. of Product (Anna Morales), Head of Platform (Luis Ortega), CTO (acting; VP Eng: Ravi Kapoor).
- Pain: search quality drops for long-tail SKUs; frequent incidents during Black Friday traffic; latency spikes on vector search.
- Regulatory/ops: handles PII in customer messages (email/phone), wants to avoid risky data egress.

Hypotheses to test with this account: 
1) They will prioritize stability and predictable unit cost over raw throughput. Pitch: Dedicated capacity + rollout policy.
2) Security (VPC + KMS) is minimum bar; emphasize Private deployment or Dedicated with data isolation.
3) A 4–6 week pilot with an instrumentation milestone (latency p95 < 200ms on 1k concurrent users) will get buy-in from Platform.
4) Dev friction matters: if we can deliver a sample route and SDK snippet in <3 days, we win the initial PO.

Value props to emphasize (condensed):
- Predictable token economics + observability (token-level cost breakdown per route).
- Autoscaling dedicated pools during traffic spikes (Black Friday resilience).
- Private/VPC options + KMS integration for PII compliance.
- Tooling: rollout A/B, canary fallback to smaller model to maintain uptime.

Subject lines / LI opener candidates (test variations):
- "Sample: 3-day spike-proof search test for Hearthline"
- "Reduce Black Friday latency spikes — quick pilot?"
- "Fast POC: secure, predictable LLM search (no data egress)"

Cold email draft — version A (short, outcome-focused):
Hi Anna —
We helped a commerce platform reduce search latency spikes by 65% during peak traffic using a small dedicated inference pool and prefix caching. Could I book 20 minutes next week to show a 3-step pilot that proves it for Hearthline?

Cold email draft — version B (developer-first, technical):
Hey Luis —
Quick note: we can stand up a sandbox route, deploy a model variant tuned for catalog search, and attach a live latency/cost dashboard in <72 hours. No data leaves your VPC if you want. Interested in a short tech call?

6-touch cadence (hypothesis):
1) Day 0: LI connection + 1-sentence value claim (subject lines above).
2) Day 3: Short email (A/B) with 2-screenshot proof (dashboard + before/after).
3) Day 7: Technical note to Head of Platform with SDK snippet and minimal infra ask.
4) Day 12: LinkedIn message or voicemail — mention upcoming Black Friday readiness window.
5) Day 20: Pricing anchor email — 6-week pilot $Xk + SLA + success metrics.
6) Day 30: Breakup note with one last evidence point and offer to introduce to an existing customer for reference.

Call script kernel (10–12 min intro call):
- 0:00–2:00 quick intros, context-setting (we're Redwood; focus on inference economics).
- 2:00–5:00 hear them — ask: "what does search failure look like for you?" and "how do you measure cost today?"
- 5:00–8:00 share a micro-case (before/after metrics from similar customer) + show a single slide of the pilot plan.
- 8:00–10:00 alignment: success metrics (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, error rate) + next technicals (access, sample data, compliance checklist).

Pilot offer (concise):
- Duration: 6 weeks (can compress to 3 wks for a small slice).
- Deliverables: Dedicated sandbox route, sample model variant (quantized), latency/cost dashboard, rollout policy, runbook + on-call during scheduled traffic test.
- Success criteria (mutually agreed): p95 latency improvement >= 30% on catalog search, cost per query within 15% of current vector-only baseline, no PII egress incidents.
- Price: $12k fixed (cover infra + eng time) + option to commit to 3-month Dedicated reserve if metrics met.

Objections anticipated (and short rebuttals):
1) "We're worried about vendor lock-in."
   - Rebuttal: Redwood exports models and routes; customers can pin model versions and we provide a staged rollback plan. Plus we offer private deployments and a portable SDK.
2) "We can't expose customer data."
   - Rebuttal: Pilot can run inside your VPC / private deployment with KMS keys. We do not persist raw PII and provide audit logs.
3) "Cost — how do we know this won't blow up token spend?"
   - Rebuttal: We'll run a cost projection using a 3-day traffic sample, plus guardrails (batching thresholds, cache TTLs) and per-route quotas.
4) "We already have an internal infra team."
   - Rebuttal: Offer a co-managed pilot: we handle runtime + ops, your infra owns networking and secrets. Knowledge transfer included.

Measurement plan (what to instrument in the trial):
- Route-level p95 latency (ms), tail latency charts by request size.
- Token consumption per route and per user session.
- Cache hit rate (prefix + KV) on catalog queries.
- Error rate and fallback events (how often we fallback to smaller model or to search-only).

Immediate to-dos (personal checklist):
- Draft email A/B for Anna + Luis (due 48h). -> JIRA: JIRA-PLAT-4471 (create ticket to track send + follow-ups).
- Build 2 slide proof deck (metrics + pilot plan) (Priya volunteer).
- Prepare SDK snippet: node/python examples for route + rolling fallback (Evan to stub).
- Prepare brief privacy sheet for Legal: includes KMS, data retention, audit logs.

Open questions / unknowns to verify before outreach:
- Who owns procurement (Finance or Platform)?
- Do they have existing commitments to another inference vendor? (check job postings, StackShare, LinkedIn).
- Typical query sizes (avg tokens) for catalog search — need sample.

Notes-to-self: keep language dev-focused for Platform leads; for Product highlight outcomes (conversion + latency). Test subject lines for urgency (Black Friday) vs curiosity ("3-day test").

Experiment tracking: tag this prospect under "atelier-2026-coldseq" in the outbound tracker and record opens/replies in CRM. If Anna replies, prioritize technical demo slot in same week.

Final reminder: avoid copying canned 'AI' fluff. Be specific (numbers, timeline, access requirements). If we can show a live dashboard within 72h after access, conversion rate increases a lot.
